title: Two Markets, Two Moods: Seoul Sinks as Wall Street Rebounds
body:
It is not every day that Seoul and New York move in opposite directions this sharply. On Tuesday, the KOSPI tumbled 3.6% to 5,648.79, and the KOSDAQ fared even worse, sliding 4.1% to 704.39. Most of the **selling pressure** came from foreign investors, who dumped a net 1.52 trillion won, while institutions sold another 511 billion won. Individual investors bought 1.66 trillion won, soaking up about four-fifths of what the others sold. Over the past 20 trading days, the KOSPI has lost 19.3%, whereas the S&P 500 has dropped only 3.2% — a **divergence** (엇갈림) that is hard to ignore.

Hours later, Wall Street told a different story. Led by a rebound in chipmakers, the Nasdaq rose 0.8% to 25,372.01 and the S&P 500 gained 0.4% to 7,568.92. Not only did the rally calm fears of a deeper tech slump, but it also pushed the VIX down 1.5% to 20.83. Apple fell 1.9% even though its quarterly revenue grew 12% to $114.5 billion, because its holiday-quarter outlook disappointed. Investors were also watching the midterm elections, with prediction markets giving Democrats nearly a 75% chance of winning the Senate.

Some analysts argue that Korean stocks now look **oversold** (과매도). If foreign selling **runs out of steam**, a sharp bounce is possible. Yet the number of investors willing to bet on that remains small, and many are **holding back** until the outlook stops **deteriorating**. What is **evident** is that the two markets are now driven by different forces, not a shared mood.
ko:
서울과 뉴욕이 이렇게 극명하게 반대로 움직이는 날은 흔치 않다. 화요일 코스피는 3.6% 급락한 5,648.79에 마감했고, 코스닥은 4.1% 내린 704.39로 더 나빴다. 매도 압력의 대부분은 외국인에게서 나왔는데, 외국인은 1조 5,200억 원어치 순매도했고 기관도 5,110억 원을 더 팔았다. 개인은 1조 6,600억 원을 사들여 다른 주체가 판 물량의 약 5분의 4를 받아냈다. 최근 20거래일 동안 코스피는 19.3% 빠진 반면 S&P500은 3.2% 하락에 그쳤다 — 무시하기 어려운 괴리다.

몇 시간 뒤 월가는 다른 이야기를 들려줬다. 반도체주 반등에 힘입어 나스닥은 0.8% 오른 25,372.01, S&P500은 0.4% 오른 7,568.92를 기록했다. 이 반등은 기술주 급락이 더 깊어질 거라는 두려움을 달랬을 뿐 아니라 VIX도 1.5% 끌어내려 20.83으로 만들었다. 애플은 분기 매출이 12% 늘어 1,145억 달러를 기록했는데도 연말 분기 전망이 실망스러워 1.9% 떨어졌다. 투자자들은 중간선거도 지켜봤는데, 예측시장은 민주당이 상원을 차지할 확률을 75% 가까이로 봤다.

일부 애널리스트는 한국 주식이 이제 과매도 상태로 보인다고 주장한다. 외국인 매도의 기세가 꺾이면 가파른 반등도 가능하다. 하지만 그쪽에 걸려는 투자자의 수는 여전히 적고, 많은 이들이 전망 악화가 멈출 때까지 매수를 미루고 있다. 분명한 것은 두 시장이 이제 같은 분위기가 아니라 서로 다른 힘에 의해 움직이고 있다는 점이다.

vocab.en_easy: A situation where many people want to sell, which pushes prices down.
vocab.ex: The selling pressure eased in the afternoon, so the index closed off its lows.

vocab.en_easy: When two things that usually move together start moving apart.
vocab.ex: There's a big divergence between what analysts say and what foreign investors actually do.

vocab.en_easy: Sold so much and so fast that the price may be lower than it should be.
vocab.ex: The stock looks oversold, but I'll wait for a clear bounce before I buy.
My running form started to deteriorate after I skipped training for a month.

vocab.en_easy: Easy to see or understand; clear.
vocab.ex: It was evident from the long line that the new café was a big hit.

vocab.en_easy: To lose energy or force and slow down.
vocab.ex: I usually run out of steam around the 8 km mark, so I'm working on my endurance.

vocab.en_easy: To stop yourself from doing something, often because you are unsure.
vocab.ex: I held back from buying more shares until the earnings report came out.

grammar.point: 강조·도치 (It is ~ that 강조구문 · Not only + 조동사 + 주어 ~, but (also) …)
grammar.quote: It is not every day that Seoul and New York move in opposite directions this sharply. / Not only did the rally calm fears of a deeper tech slump, but it also pushed the VIX down 1.5% to 20.83.
grammar.explain_ko: ① It is + 강조할 말 + that 나머지: 문장의 한 부분을 앞으로 끌어내 강조한다(It is not every day that ~ = ~하는 날은 흔치 않다, 관용 표현). ② Not only 같은 부정어가 문장 맨 앞에 오면 의문문 어순으로 도치: 일반동사 과거면 did + 주어 + 동사원형(Not only did the rally calm ✓ / Not only the rally calmed ✗). be동사면 Not only was it ~. 수능 어법 단골: 도치 뒤 동사원형·조동사 자리.
examples: Only when the outlook improves will foreign investors return.
(OPIc) Not only is the café close to my place, but it also has the best cold brew in my neighborhood.

grammar.point: 수 일치 (the number of + 복수명사 → 단수동사 · 관계사절 사이에 끼인 주어)
grammar.quote: Yet the number of investors willing to bet on that remains small, … / Most of the selling pressure came from foreign investors, …
grammar.explain_ko: the number of + 복수명사는 '~의 수'(하나의 숫자)라 단수동사(remains ✓, remain ✗). 반대로 a number of + 복수명사는 '많은 ~'이라 복수동사(A number of investors are …). 부분표현 most of / some of / half of 는 of 뒤 명사에 맞춘다: most of the pressure(불가산) → 단수, most of the investors → 복수. 주어와 동사 사이에 willing to ~ 같은 수식어가 길게 끼어도 진짜 주어(the number)를 찾아라.
examples: The number of foreign buyers has dropped, while a number of retail investors are buying the dip.
(OPIc) The number of cafés in my neighborhood has doubled, and most of them are open until midnight.

tense.sentence: Over the past 20 trading days, the KOSPI has lost 19.3%, whereas the S&P 500 has dropped only 3.2%.
tense.why_ko: '지난 20거래일 동안(over the past ~)' — 과거에서 지금까지 이어진 기간의 누적 결과라 현재완료.

tense.sentence: Apple fell 1.9% even though its quarterly revenue grew 12% to $114.5 billion, because its holiday-quarter outlook disappointed.
tense.why_ko: 화요일 하루에 끝난 사건(주가 하락)과 이미 발표된 실적을 말하므로 과거형. 기간 표현이 없으니 현재완료 ✗.

review.q: Even as the KOSPI slid 3.6%, a few defensive stocks such as telecoms ______ surprisingly well.
review.exp_ko: hold up = (어려운 상황에서도) 잘 버티다. 'Even as(~하는 와중에도) + surprisingly well'과 어울리는 건 버텼다. gave in(굴복했다)·broke down(무너졌다)은 well 과 모순, fell through(계획이 무산되다)는 주가 주어와 안 맞음.

review.q: The 4% drop at the open looked like a knee-jerk reaction, and prices had recovered by noon. 밑줄 친 knee-jerk 와 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은?
review.exp_ko: knee-jerk = 무릎 반사처럼 '생각 없이 즉각적인'. 정오에 회복했다는 문맥도 '감정적 과잉반응'을 뒷받침. delayed(지연된)·calculated(계산된)는 반대 성격, lasting(지속되는)은 정오 회복과 모순.

review.q: I couldn't decide between the two chip stocks, so I ______ by buying a small amount of each.
review.exp_ko: hedge one's bets = 한쪽에 몰빵하지 않고 양쪽에 나눠 걸다 → '둘 다 조금씩 샀다'와 정확히 일치. jumped the gun(성급하게 먼저 움직였다)·cut it close(아슬아슬했다)·called it a day(그만 마쳤다)는 '나눠 사기'를 설명 못 함.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"Foreign investors have been selling for weeks, but analysts say that if their selling ______, Korean stocks could bounce sharply."
quiz.exp_ko: '외국인 매도가 ~하면 → 급반등 가능'이므로 매도의 힘이 빠져야 한다 → runs out of steam(기세가 꺾이다). picks up speed·gains momentum(속도·탄력이 붙다)은 매도가 더 거세진다는 뜻이라 반등 조건과 반대, holds its ground(버티다·유지하다)는 매도가 계속된다는 뜻.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"①Led by chipmakers, the Nasdaq rose 0.8%. ②Not only the rally calmed fears of a tech slump, but it also pushed the VIX lower. Yet the number of investors willing to buy Korean stocks ③remains small, and many ④are holding back."
choices: ② Not only the rally calmed
quiz.exp_ko: Not only 가 문장 앞에 오면 도치 → Not only did the rally calm ✓. ① 나스닥이 반도체주에 '이끌린' 수동 관계라 과거분사 Led ✓ ③ the number of + 복수명사 = '수'(단수) → remains ✓ ④ many(= many investors, 복수) → are holding ✓.

quiz.q: [빈칸 추론] 윗글의 마지막 문장 "What is evident is that ______."의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Korean stocks have become cheap enough to attract foreign buyers again
the strength of U.S. chip stocks will soon spread to the Korean market
individual investors are selling faster than foreign investors are buying
the two markets are now driven by different forces, not a shared mood
quiz.exp_ko: 글 전체가 '같은 날 서울은 급락, 뉴욕은 반등 + 20일 −19.3% vs −3.2% 괴리'를 말하므로 결론은 '두 시장이 서로 다른 힘으로 움직인다'. ① 외국인은 여전히 팔고 있고 '과매도' 주장은 일부 애널리스트 의견일 뿐 ② 미국 강세가 번질 거라는 근거 없음(오히려 괴리 강조) ③ 개인은 '샀고' 외국인이 '팔았다' — 주체·방향이 뒤바뀜.

choices: 개인의 순매수액은 외국인과 기관 순매도 합계의 80%를 넘었다.
코스닥의 하락률은 코스피 하락률보다 1%p 이상 컸다.
애플의 매출 증가율은 VIX 하락률의 10배를 넘었다.

talk.topic: Foreigners sell, retail buys — 코스피 −3.6% 날 외국인 1.5조 팔고 개인이 받았다
talk.setting_ko: 수요일 아침 회사 탕비실. 주식을 하는 동료 둘이 어제 코스피 급락과 밤사이 미국 반등을 이야기한다.

dialogue.en: Did you see the KOSPI yesterday? Down 3.6%. And then the Nasdaq goes up almost 1% overnight. Unreal.
dialogue.ko: 어제 코스피 봤어? 3.6% 빠졌어. 그러고 밤에 나스닥은 1% 가까이 오르고. 말이 안 돼.

dialogue.en: Yeah, foreigners keep pulling out of Korea. They sold like 1.5 trillion won in one day.
dialogue.ko: 응, 외국인이 계속 한국에서 빠져나가. 하루에 1조 5천억 원쯤 팔았대.

dialogue.en: And retail investors picked up the slack, right? They bought about 1.7 trillion.
I know. Part of me likes going against the crowd, but catching every dip is exhausting.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까. 남들 반대로 가는 게 좋긴 한데, 떨어질 때마다 받는 건 진이 빠져.

dialogue.en: Was there a bright spot at all? Anything?
Well, U.S. chip stocks bounced, so maybe our chip names get a little lift today.
dialogue.ko: 음, 미국 반도체주가 반등했으니까 오늘 우리 반도체도 좀 오를 수도.

dialogue.en: Maybe. Plus the midterm results are coming in today. Time will tell.
dialogue.ko: 그럴지도. 게다가 오늘 중간선거 결과도 나오고. 두고 봐야지.

dialogue.en: Exactly. I'm just not adding anything until the foreigners stop selling.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 난 외국인 매도가 멈출 때까지 더 안 살 거야.

expressions.ex: Foreign funds pulled out of emerging markets last month.

expressions.ko: (다른 사람이 못 한 몫을) 메우다, 떠맡다
expressions.when_ko: 누군가 빠진 자리를 다른 사람이 채울 때 — 직장·팀 운동에도
expressions.ex: When my coworker was on vacation, I had to pick up the slack.

expressions.when_ko: 역발상 투자·남들과 다른 선택을 말할 때
expressions.ex: I like to go against the crowd and visit Busan in winter, when it's quiet.

expressions.ko: (나쁜 상황 속) 좋은 점, 한 줄기 빛
expressions.when_ko: 전반적으로 나쁜 가운데 좋은 부분을 짚을 때
expressions.ex: The one bright spot of my trip was the amazing street food.

expressions.ko: 시간이 지나 봐야 알지. / 두고 보면 알겠지.
expressions.when_ko: 결과를 아직 알 수 없을 때 말을 마무리하는 한 줄
expressions.ex: Will this new running shoe help my knees? Time will tell.

your_turn.q_en: When foreign investors are selling heavily, would you buy along with retail investors or wait? Why?
your_turn.hint_ko: go against the crowd · pull out of · Time will tell 중 2개 + 내 원칙 한 줄(분할 매수·관망 등)
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, I'd probably wait a little. I know some people like to go against the crowd and buy when everyone's selling, but when foreigners pull out of the market this fast, it usually keeps going for a while. So I'd split my cash and buy only a small amount at a time. Will that work? Time will tell.

talk.topic: 친구와 10K 마라톤 대회 신청하기 (Background Survey #46 조깅)
talk.setting_ko: 저녁 한강 조깅 후 벤치에서 쉬며, 친구가 다음 달 10K 대회에 같이 나가자고 한다.

dialogue.en: Hey, there's a 10K race next month along the river. Want to sign up for it with me?
dialogue.ko: 야, 다음 달에 강변에서 10K 대회 있대. 나랑 같이 신청할래?

dialogue.en: A 10K? I don't know. I'm kind of out of shape these days.
dialogue.ko: 10K? 글쎄. 나 요즘 몸이 좀 많이 무뎌졌어.

dialogue.en: You just ran 5K with me! We can work up to 10K over the next four weeks.
dialogue.ko: 방금 나랑 5K 뛰었잖아! 앞으로 4주 동안 10K까지 차근차근 늘리면 돼.

dialogue.en: Hmm, what if I get cold feet the week before?
dialogue.ko: 음, 대회 일주일 전에 겁먹고 빠지고 싶어지면 어떡해?

dialogue.en: Then I'll drag you out of bed myself. Come on, the registration fee is only 30,000 won.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 내가 직접 침대에서 끌어낼게. 에이, 참가비 3만 원밖에 안 해.

dialogue.en: Okay, okay. I'm in if you're in. But we're doing long runs on Saturdays.
dialogue.ko: 알았어, 알았어. 너 하면 나도 할게. 대신 토요일마다 장거리 뛰는 거다.

dialogue.en: Deal. Let's sign up tonight before it fills up.
dialogue.ko: 콜. 마감되기 전에 오늘 밤에 신청하자.

expressions.when_ko: 대회·수업·헬스장 등록을 말할 때 — OPIc 운동 주제 필수
expressions.ex: I signed up for a spinning class at my gym last month.

expressions.when_ko: 한동안 운동을 쉬어 체력이 약해졌을 때
expressions.ex: I was really out of shape after the holidays, so I started jogging again.

expressions.when_ko: 운동량·무게·거리를 점진적으로 늘릴 때(progressive overload와 같은 맥락)
expressions.ex: I started with 40 kg on the squat and worked up to 80 kg in six months.

expressions.when_ko: 중요한 일 직전에 자신이 없어질 때
expressions.ex: I almost got cold feet before my first race, but I'm glad I ran it.
A trip to Jeju next month? I'm in if you're in.

your_turn.q_en: Have you ever signed up for a race or a fitness challenge? How did you prepare for it?
your_turn.hint_ko: sign up for · work up to · get cold feet 중 2개 + 준비 과정 2단계(처음엔 ~, 나중엔 ~)
your_turn.sample_answer: Yeah, a couple of years ago I signed up for a 10K race with my coworkers. At first, I could barely run 3 km without stopping, so I worked up to 10 km little by little, adding about one kilometer every week. I almost got cold feet the night before, but on race day the crowd was so energetic that I finished in under an hour.

opic.survey_topic: 카페/커피전문점 (Background Survey #12) · 수요일 콤보: 비교·변화 — 묘사 → 카페의 변화(과거 vs 현재) → 사람들의 커피 문화 변화(사회)

combo.q_en: You indicated in the survey that you go to coffee shops. Tell me about your favorite coffee shop. Where is it, what does it look like, and why do you like going there?
combo.q_ko: 설문에서 커피전문점에 간다고 하셨네요. 가장 좋아하는 카페에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼고, 왜 그곳에 가는 걸 좋아하나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(카페 이름·위치 한 줄) → 본문 3포인트: ① 위치·외관(골목, 2층, 큰 창) ② 내부 묘사(오감 — 커피 향·음악·조명·좌석) ③ 좋아하는 이유(나만의 루틴·감정) → 마무리(추천 한 줄). 90초. IH/AL 포인트: 형용사 나열이 아니라 '공간을 걸어 들어가듯' 순서대로 묘사, 감정 한 줄, 자기수정 1회.
combo.model_answer: Okay, so my favorite coffee shop is a small place called Moonbean. It's about five minutes from my apartment, tucked away in a quiet alley, so most people just walk right past it. From the outside, it doesn't look like much — just a wooden door and a tiny sign — but once you step inside, it's a whole different world. The first thing you notice is the smell of freshly roasted beans, because they actually roast their own coffee in the back. There are big windows on one side, so it's really bright in the afternoon, and they always play this soft jazz, not too loud. There are maybe, um, eight or nine tables? Actually, closer to ten. My favorite spot is the corner seat by the window. Why do I like it so much? Well, it's where I go to recharge. I usually go there on Sunday mornings, order a hand-drip coffee, and just read or check the market news without anyone bothering me. It's kind of my little hideout. Honestly, if you ever visit my neighborhood, you have to check it out.

key_phrases.en: It doesn't look like much from the outside, but ~
The first thing you notice is ~
It's kind of my little hideout.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 'big, nice, quiet' 나열 → IH는 들어가는 동선 순서 묘사 → AL은 'Why do I like it so much? Well, ~'처럼 스스로 질문하고 답하며 감정·이유까지 한 문단으로.

combo.q_en: How have coffee shops changed since you first started going to them? What were they like back then, and how are they different now? Please give me as many details as possible.
combo.q_ko: 처음 카페에 다니기 시작했을 때와 비교해 카페는 어떻게 바뀌었나요? 그때는 어땠고, 지금은 어떻게 다른가요? 최대한 자세히 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(처음 다닌 시기 — 대학 때 등) → 본문: 과거 2포인트(메뉴·분위기) ↔ 현재 2포인트(키오스크·디저트·공부 카페) → 마무리(내 생각: 좋아진 점 + 아쉬운 점). 90초~2분. IH/AL 포인트: 과거는 used to / would, 현재는 현재형·현재완료(have become) — 시제 전환이 채점 핵심. 'compared to ~, ~'로 대비를 명확히.
combo.model_answer: Hmm, let me think. I first started going to cafés when I was in college, so that's, what, about ten years ago? Back then, cafés were mostly just places to grab a coffee and chat with friends. The menus were pretty simple — you'd have an Americano, a latte, maybe a caramel macchiato, and that was it. And you'd always order from a person at the counter. These days, though, things have changed a lot. First of all, a lot of cafés have kiosks now, so you barely talk to anyone. I mean, it's convenient, but it feels a bit cold sometimes. Second, the menus have become way more creative. There are seasonal drinks, fancy desserts, even cafés that only sell one kind of cake. And compared to before, so many people use cafés as offices. You see people with laptops everywhere, studying or working for hours. Personally, I think the coffee itself is much better now, but I kind of miss the old, chatty atmosphere. It used to feel more like a hangout, and now it feels more like a workspace.

key_phrases.en: These days, though, things have changed a lot.
It's convenient, but it feels a bit cold.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '예전엔 A, 지금은 B' 한 줄 비교 → IH는 과거(used to/would)·현재(have become) 시제를 정확히 바꿔 2포인트씩 → AL은 마지막에 'It used to feel like ~, and now it feels like ~'로 변화를 한 문장으로 요약하며 내 평가까지.

combo.q_en: Let's talk about coffee culture in your country. How have people's coffee habits changed over the years? What did people use to do, and what do they do now? Why do you think these changes happened?
combo.q_ko: 당신 나라의 커피 문화에 대해 이야기해 봅시다. 사람들의 커피 습관은 몇 년 사이 어떻게 바뀌었나요? 예전엔 어땠고 지금은 어떤가요? 왜 이런 변화가 생겼다고 생각하나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(한국 = 커피 공화국 한 줄) → 본문: ① 예전(믹스커피·다방·자판기) ② 지금(아이스 아메리카노·하루 2~3잔·저가 커피 체인) ③ 이유 2개(바쁜 직장 문화·카페가 사교 공간이 됨) → 마무리(나도 그 일부라는 자기 이야기). 2분. IH/AL 포인트: 사회 변화 질문은 '이유'가 핵심 — I think it's because ~ / Another reason is that ~ 로 원인 2개를 분명히.
combo.model_answer: Oh, Korea is basically a coffee nation now, so there's a lot to say. Well, when I was a kid, most adults drank instant coffee — you know, those little yellow coffee mix sticks. My dad used to have two or three of them every day at work, from a paper cup. Going to a café wasn't really a daily thing back then; it was more for dates or special meetings. Now, it's totally different. People drink iced Americanos all year round, even in the middle of winter, which still surprises my foreign friends. And a lot of office workers grab a coffee on the way to work and another one after lunch, almost like a ritual. Why did this happen? I think it's mainly because work life is so busy here, and coffee is how people keep going. Another reason is that cafés have become social spaces — they're where people meet, study, and even work. Also, cheap coffee chains have popped up everywhere, so a cup costs only about two thousand won. I'm guilty of it too, actually — I can't start my day without one.

key_phrases.en: ~ is basically a coffee nation now.
It wasn't really a daily thing back then.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 변화만 말하고 끝 → IH는 '왜?'에 이유 2개 → AL은 사회적 원인(직장 문화·가격) + 내 경험(I'm guilty of it too)까지 엮어 개인↔사회를 오가는 문단.

opic.practice_ko: 2번 문항을 녹음 1회 → 다시 들으며 과거(used to/would)와 현재(have become/these days) 시제가 섞인 곳을 체크 → 'Compared to before'·'I kind of miss' 넣어 2분 맞춰 재녹음.
